title: Connect runs the drive app when no document is selected and hands over to the registered editor when one is opened
content:
## Selection is the switch

An **editor** renders the inside of one document — one task, one contract, one budget row. A **drive app** renders the outside: the whole drive, a list of every task, a dashboard composing many documents into one view.

The rule that decides which one runs is not configuration, it is selection state. When a user has a drive open with **no document selected**, Connect runs the drive app. When they **open a specific document**, the registered editor for that document's type takes over — and the drive app can still wrap it as a shell rather than being replaced outright.

## Picking the right one

The sharp line follows from the rule:

| Goal | Right tool |
| --- | --- |
| Kanban board over every task document in a drive | drive app |
| Rich form for filling out one contract | editor |
| Custom file-tree sidebar for a drive | drive app |
| Render and edit one specific task | editor |

Anything cross-document — navigation, aggregation, a workflow screen spanning several documents — is drive-app work. Anything scoped to a single document's fields is editor work. Getting this backwards is the usual reason a "dashboard editor" ends up needing hooks it cannot legitimately call: an editor is handed one document, so reaching sideways into the whole drive from inside one is fighting the architecture.

## Why it matters for shipping products

Connect's default drive view is a generic folder tree, which is fine for storage and wrong for a product. Replacing that view is exactly what a drive app is for. The combination — drive app owning navigation and cross-document views, editors owning each detail view — covers the full surface area of a real frontend without leaving Connect and without building a separate SPA.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/02-Learn/05-connect/02-drive-apps.mdx (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: Selection is the switch: drive open with nothing selected renders the drive app; opening a document mounts its editor, which the drive app can still wrap as a shell.
